items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I met Ellington the night I graduated from prep school... he said, 'Miss Enzinger, what are your plans?'

ctx.x: Now you, you were pretty into the Ellington band too.

That was my main band, and so when Bob and I came into each other’s lives there were two emerging — the great marriage of the Ellingtons and the Basies. Yes. I met Ellington the night I graduated from prep school. And that was in June of 1936. And we were all dressed up in party clothes, you know it was graduation night. And he said, “where do you want to go?” Well Ellington was playing a two week engagement at the Congress Hotel in Chicago. So I said, “I’d like to go and hear Ellington.” Because I’d had all his…

Ellington’s father. And he only had lived with him I think during a very brief period. It was fewer than six months. But that was just that little gap there that he’d moved into Ellington’s apartment. So he said, I said, “he told me to come by.” He said, “fine, I’ll go get him.” Well I mean the curtains were drawn, it was like midnight in there you know, ‘cause it was to them, midnight. It was very dark in the living room.
